question_type: Share of one month's savings-bond redemptions (all series) that is the 'Accrued discount' component, with the column named by an obfuscated paraphrase ('elapsed value buildup from the original price markdown'); one row, two cells, percent to 2 decimals
decisive_step: Mapping the paraphrase to the 'Redemptions > Accrued discount' column (not the sales-side 'Accrued discount' column two columns to the left, and not the by-series Table 3 whose Dec 1961 OCR is misaligned) of Table 2 'Sales and Redemptions by Periods, All Series Combined', October 1961 row, and dividing by 'Redemptions > Total'. The reference made it at worklog Step 0 and Step 4 (treasury_bulletin_1961_12.txt:2913 header, :2942 row) and confirmed no vintage conflict across the 8 printings 1961_12..1962_07 (worklog Step 7). Vintage is irrelevant here: every printing agrees.

It correctly identified the redemption-side accrued-discount column and the total (a[36]). Three printings calls failed on the column hint (a[38], a[42], a[54]) before 'Accrued discount' (a[52]) and 'Redemptions 1/ > Total' (a[56]) listed 8 identical printings; calc at a[58]; answered with the percent sign.

smallest_change.change: printings --col matching: strip footnote marks (regex '\s*\d{1,2}/' anywhere in the label, not only trailing) from both the printed label and the hint before the substring test in otables.printings_data (line 'col_hint not in norm(lab)'), and when nothing matches print the table's column labels instead of the bare 'no matching row/column found', e.g.: 'no column contains "redemptions > total"; columns in treasury_bulletin_1962_07.txt:3065 are: c1 Sales 1/ | c2 Accrued discount | c3 Sales plus accrued discount | c4 Redemptions 1/ > Total | c5 Redemptions 1/ > Sales price 2/ | c6 Redemptions 1/ > Accrued discount 2/ | ...'. Same normalisation for the --table hint ('Table 2 in ...' should match a numbered table by its number and section).

notes: The trap on this question is the by-series table in the Dec 1961 issue, whose OCR shifts the accrued-discount cell (b[10] showed it: a one-digit accrued value and spurious 'REVISED/DIFFERS' summary lines). printings' SUMMARY flagged those as revisions rather than as a column shift; a per-row identity check (sales price + accrued discount = total, which Table 2's NOTES already report as 'identity ... on 27/27 rows' at a[44]) applied inside printings would label such printings 'IDENTITY FAILS - misaligned' instead of 'REVISED'. Also worth noting: printings reports 'latest printing 1962_07' because later issues drop the 1961 months; a[45]-[51] and c[34] both spent steps wondering whether later issues were missing - a one-line 'row not printed in 1962_08..1963_10 (table window moved on)' would settle that. No v8 per-question analysis exists for this question (all v8 arms were right; officeqa-divergence-analysis/per-question/022.json is absent).
